buyer: Ambitious practice owners wanting to develop their own schemes
pain: They can design it but cannot fund, model or structure it
v1: A feasibility and funding structure for one architect's first scheme
verdict: Emotionally compelling and perfectly matched, but the client population is tiny and cash-poor.

why.distribution: Reachable directly, but only a small minority of architects actually attempt this.
why.demand: Inferred from the profession's ambition, not from anyone's budget.
why.fmf: She has made a version of this journey herself - unusually credible guidance.
why.revenue_structure: One engagement per architect, essentially once in their career.
why.defensibility: Very few advisors can speak both languages.
why.time_to_revenue: 3-6 months to find the first genuine case.
why.ceiling: £9k x 22 clients = £198k, and there are not twenty-two architects a year doing this who can pay.

ceiling_arithmetic: £9k x 22 clients = £198k. The realistic annual population of architects starting a first development and able to pay is single digits. Realistic: 2-3 = £18-27k.
carries: A story only she can tell, and clients who would genuinely value her.
kills: Market size. The buyer population is measured in dozens nationally and most cannot pay.
test: Ask her architecture network how many are actively trying to develop.
